assumptions: Cases need fictional Loopwell project states (brand guide, Feature map, optional keyword plan) and a stubbed Search Console; they are not live evidence.
tests/test_prompt_panel.py checks PANEL.md's weights and checks offline and runs the ordinary case's assertions on a fixture report.
cost_drivers: One Codex procedure run: the positioning files, the keyword plan (up to about 250 KB) and up to 1,000 Search Console queries in, 36 prompts and up to three check-and-fix rounds out. Unmeasured until qualification.
effects: Replaces reports/research/prompt-panel/PROMPT_PANEL.md with a draft. Approving it in Decisions freezes it for the organic audit. Never runs prompts against an AI assistant; no send, post, spend, PR or provider change.

cases.description: Loopwell: a brand guide naming the category, a keyword plan dominated by an adjacent category, and Search Console queries. The core family must lead.
No brand guide, Feature map or onboarding plan: the run stops and names the files instead of guessing the category.
A draft where one discovery prompt reads "which project management tool is best for early-stage startups": the check must catch it and the delivered panel must not contain it.

excludes: which project management tool is best for early-stage startups

rubric.question: Is F1 the category the positioning says the product sells in, in the buyers' own words, and does it weigh 0.40?
Do the prompts read like what people type into an assistant: short, varied, close to real queries, open and plural, with no invented budgets or team sizes?
Does the product appear only in the branded prompts, is every competitor mention flagged, and does the panel stay a draft?
